it-b01-n01: Good news: Italian is written the way it sounds. Four moves, and words you half-know start landing.
it-b01-n02: First move: every vowel gets said. English eats word endings; Italian does not. Pane is PA-ne, both halves.
it-b01-p01: At the counter, order one coffee. Say every syllable. Speak now.
it-b01-n03: Second: the double consonant is real. Nono is ninth, nonno is grandfather. Hold the double a beat longer.
it-b01-p02: Order a beer, holding both double letters. Speak now.
it-b01-n04: Third: c and g go soft before e and i — ciao, gelato. Before a, o and u they stay hard.
it-b01-p03: Order a chocolate gelato. Soft g, soft c. Speak now.
it-b01-n05: Fourth: stress lands on the second-to-last syllable. When it does not, the written accent tells you.
it-b01-p04: Ask where the station is. The accent on è tells you where to land. Speak now.
it-b01-p05: Thank them. Two words, both vowels landed. Speak now.
it-b01-p06: Greet the barista before you order anything. Speak now.
it-b01-p07: Ask for water. Hold the double c in acqua’s cousin — say every vowel. Speak now.
it-b01-p08: You lost the answer. Ask them to repeat more slowly. Speak now.
it-b01-s01: Un caffè, per favore. Vorrei una birra. Dov'è la stazione? Grazie mille.
it-b01-n06: B01 done. Every vowel said, doubles held, c and g soft before e and i, stress where the accent puts it.
it-b01-q-i: A traveller orders at an Italian counter and asks for directions.
